title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 371
paragraphs: This shrine, then, of all the things I saw in that temple, is the most marvelous, and next to it comes the island called Chemmis. It lies in a deep, broad lake beside the temple at Buto, and the Egyptians say that this island is a floating island. I myself did not see it either floating about or moved from its place, and I am astonished to hear of it, wondering whether it really is a floating island. On this island of which I speak there is a great temple-house of Apollo, and three separate altars are set up within, and many palm trees and other trees are planted there, some fruit-bearing and some not. The Egyptians, when they say that it floats, add this story: on this island, which formerly was not floating, Leto, being one of the eight gods who came into existence first, and dwelling in the city of Buto where she has her oracle, received Apollo from Isis as a charge and preserved him, concealing him on the island now said to be floating, at the time when Typhon came in pursuit, searching everywhere, desiring to find the son of Osiris. They say that Apollo and Artemis are the children of Dionysos and Isis, and that Leto became their nurse and protector; and in the Egyptian tongue Apollo is Oros, Demeter is Isis, and Artemis is Bubastis. From this story and from no other Aeschylus son of Euphorion took what I am about to say, in which he differs from all earlier poets: he represented Artemis as the daughter of Demeter. For this reason, they say, the island became a floating one.
Such is the story they tell;
